stem: $ABCD$ is a kite with $AB = AD$ and $CB = CD$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $E$. $B\hat{A}D = {=p}^\circ$. Calculate the size of $A\hat{B}D$, in degrees.
solution: $AC$ is the diagonal between the equal sides $AB$ and $AD$, so it bisects $B\hat{A}D$: $B\hat{A}E = {=p}^\circ \div 2 = {=h}^\circ$.
The diagonals of a kite intersect at right angles, so $A\hat{E}B = 90^\circ$.
The angles of $\triangle ABE$ add up to $180^\circ$: $A\hat{B}E = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - {=h}^\circ = {=t}^\circ$.
notes: Standard: combines two of the three book properties (the diagonal between the equal sides bisects the interior angle; the diagonals meet at right angles) with the triangle angle sum. p is built as 2h so the half-angle is a whole number. The answer also equals (180 - p)/2 by the isosceles triangle ABD, so a solver using either route agrees. Convex kite assumed (the diagonals intersect at E).
